units.title: Sparkling wines

evidencePrompts.prompt: Describe what you actually saw, smelled and tasted. Include the mousse or bubbles and the wine's structure.
Justify your quality judgement with specific balance, intensity, complexity and finish evidence.
Explain your drinking-window and ageing judgement from the wine in the glass. What might develop, and what might limit it?
Which observed clues may support a sparkling style or production method? Separate what you sensed from any production inference.
Which conclusion is least secure? Name an observation or alternative explanation that could change it.

units.comparisonPrompt: Compare all three sparkling wines using observed mousse, aromas, structure, quality and ageing potential. Explain the evidence behind the differences.
units.selfReviewPrompt: Review your three conclusions: which observations support them, and which observations or alternative explanations weaken them?

units.title: Fortified wines

evidencePrompts.prompt: Describe what you actually saw, smelled and tasted, including sweetness, alcohol, structure and flavour development.
Justify your quality judgement with specific balance, intensity, complexity and finish evidence.
Explain your drinking-window and ageing judgement from the wine in the glass. What might develop, and what might limit it?
Which observed clues may support a fortification or maturation style? Separate sensory evidence from a production inference.
Which conclusion is least secure? Name an observation or alternative explanation that could change it.

units.comparisonPrompt: Compare all three fortified wines using observed sweetness, alcohol, maturation clues, structure, quality and ageing potential. Explain the evidence behind the differences.
units.selfReviewPrompt: Review your three conclusions: which observations support them, and which observations or alternative explanations weaken them?

units.title: Still wines of the world

evidencePrompts.prompt: Record the appearance, aromas, flavours and structure you observed in this still wine. Distinguish your observations from any information supplied about the bottle.
Explain your quality conclusion using the wine's balance, flavour intensity, complexity and finish. Which specific observations strengthen or weaken that conclusion?

Describe when you would drink this wine and whether further ageing might improve it. Support your judgement with observed fruit, structure and development, and acknowledge what the glass cannot establish.
Explain which observed clues could support a grape, growing environment or winemaking hypothesis. Separate sensory evidence from supplied identity, and consider a plausible alternative.
Identify the least secure part of your conclusion. Explain an alternative interpretation or further information that could change your reasoning; tasting alone cannot authenticate an origin or label.

units.comparisonPrompt: Compare the three actual still wines using their observed aromas, flavours, structure, quality and potential development. Explain the evidence behind their differences and any tentative commonality; identify where supplied bottle information influenced your interpretation.
units.selfReviewPrompt: Reconsider the evidence for each wine and your three-wine comparison. Identify a specific weak inference, a plausible alternative and what you would check or practise next. Your review records reasoning, not an independently assessed tasting result.
